title: One Eruption Made a Mountain 1,300 Feet Shorter

scenes.text: One eruption blew 1,300 feet off the top of a mountain.
An earthquake collapsed the north side. It was the largest landslide in recorded history.
The peak dropped from 9,677 feet to 8,365 feet.
Over five hundred million tons of ash fell across more than 22,000 square miles.
One day, one volcano, and a mountain 1,300 feet shorter.

description:
Mount St. Helens lost about 1,300 feet of its summit in the eruption of May 18th, 1980.
It caused the largest landslide in recorded history and dropped about 540 million tons of ash.
Have you ever seen a volcano in person?
